source.name: fn_FormatCustomerName

assumptions: NVARCHAR(100) mapped to VARCHAR(100) - PostgreSQL VARCHAR is Unicode-capable by default
NVARCHAR(201) mapped to VARCHAR(201) for return type
Function marked as IMMUTABLE since it has no side effects and returns consistent results for the same inputs
ISNULL() converted to COALESCE() which is functionally equivalent
String concatenation operator '+' converted to PostgreSQL '||' operator
Parameter names prefixed with 'p_' to follow PostgreSQL naming conventions and avoid reserved word conflicts
SQL Server SCHEMABINDING not applicable - PostgreSQL functions reference objects by their current definition

reviewFlags.reason: Verify that VARCHAR(201) provides sufficient length for all expected customer name combinations. The original calculation (100 + 100 + 1 for comma-space) is preserved.
Confirm that empty string handling matches business requirements when either FirstName or LastName is NULL. This will produce results like ', John' or 'Doe, ' for NULL values.

compatibilityNotes.description: SQL Server NVARCHAR uses UTF-16 encoding while PostgreSQL VARCHAR uses the database encoding (typically UTF-8). This should not affect functionality but may impact storage size.
Function marked as IMMUTABLE for optimal query optimization. This assumes the function will always return the same result for the same input parameters.
COALESCE and ISNULL are functionally equivalent for this use case. Both return the first non-NULL value or the default empty string.
